problem: Consider the section of the parabola ${x}^{2}-4y=4$ that lies in the first quadrant.  Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$  and that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=3$ on the parabola at the point where $y=3,$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.
worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4y & =4 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}-4y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(4y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x)-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot 4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=3$ and $y=3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x)-(3)\cdot 4 & =0 \\ 2x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-12 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $x,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $y=3$ into the equation of  the parabola.  

At the point where $y=3,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4y & =4 \\ {x}^{2}-4\cdot (3) & =4 \\ {x}^{2}-12 & =4 \\ {x}^{2} & =16 \\ x & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used $x>0$ since we're only interested in the  first  quadrant. 

Finally, substituting $x=4,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-12 & =0 \\ 8\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =12 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{12}{8} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
